video_title: How a Top 100 Hyperliquid Trader Finds the Next Big Trade
gist: Top-100 Hyperliquid trader Cool Crypto explains a survival-first approach (≤1x leverage, perps for hedging, options for thesis expression), argues buyback-driven revenue tokens like HYPE and Derive have fundamental floors while Zcash is a crowded, reflexive asset best played via options, favors Lighter over Hyperliquid for 3-6 months but HYPE long term, and expects crypto options volume to 5-10x with Derive losing share.

insights.claim: A top-100 Hyperliquid P&L trader attributes leaderboard rank mainly to avoiding blowups: he almost never uses more than 1x leverage across the whole portfolio, arguing crypto's big dislocations reward whoever simply survives to exploit them.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Position sizing and survival matter more than hit rate in crypto; cap portfolio-level leverage to stay alive for dislocations.
insights.quote: I literally never use more than 1x leverage on like the entire portfolio or incredibly rarely.

insights.claim: Much of the guest's Hyperliquid perp P&L came from repeatedly hedging spot HYPE holdings with perp shorts at identified local tops and buying back lower, rather than from any single big directional short; home runs came from spot holdings like Derive and Kinetic.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: A spot-core plus perp-hedge overlay can harvest volatility on a long-term holding without selling it.

insights.claim: Perp leaderboards and whale-watching carry limited signal because observers can't see a trader's offsetting positions elsewhere; a 'massive $200M Bitcoin short' may just be a delta-neutral funding-rate arbitrage fund like Brax Capital.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Don't copy-trade or read whale shorts as directional without checking whether they are funding-farming hedges.
insights.quote: that's just like a Brax Capital this Delta neutral like funding rate arbitrage fund

insights.claim: After a deep dive on tools like Hyperdash's copy-trade ratings, the guest found little consistent signal broadly, but he monitors the biggest holders of a ticker when already in a large position to spot TWAP exits that might change where he places limit orders.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Use on-chain position data as a risk-management/execution tool after entry, not as an entry signal.

insights.claim: For technical analysis, traders should watch the same widely-followed levels everyone else does (50-week and 200-day moving averages, even Fibonacci levels) because crowd behavior gives them some predictive power, while esoteric backtested indicators are mostly overfit.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Anchor TA to consensus levels; treat bespoke indicator backtests with suspicion of overfitting.
insights.quote: it has like no predictive power. It's all just back. It's all just overfitting.

insights.claim: The guest inverts this for fundamentals: edge comes from seeing fundamental data nobody else is looking at yet, and he's willing to be early by months when buybacks will force the mispricing into price anyway.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Seek differentiated fundamental work, consensus technicals.

insights.claim: The 'revenue meta' (rotation into revenue-generating tokens) has largely played out in 2026 with Pump and Hyperliquid generating heavy revenue, after years where the guest was early and wrong calling tokens like GMX cheap on P/E while capital flowed to meme coins.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Fundamentally-valued DeFi tokens have re-rated; the easy part of the revenue-meta trade may be behind us.

insights.claim: Recent US midterm results could drive a rotation out of revenue-meta tokens, which are more regulation-sensitive, into store-of-value tokens like Bitcoin and Zcash, mirroring gold's rally on expectations of lower rates and expanded spending.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Watch relative strength of BTC/ZEC vs HYPE/PUMP as a read on the post-midterm regulatory/fiscal regime.
insights.quote: rates down spending bazooka to infinity back on um and so that's more favorable and more supportive of the store of value assets

insights.claim: Despite near-term rotation risk, the guest still expects a pronounced long-run 'flight to fundamentals' in crypto where tokens are judged on actual revenue.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Near-term rotation doesn't break the structural revenue-meta thesis.

insights.claim: The 'either you are money or you make money' binary is an oversimplification: Ethereum sits in between as a credibly neutral settlement layer whose value depends on adoption Lindiness, and tokens with poor revenue-to-float ratios need an external non-sentiment value source to survive.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Tokens that are neither SoV nor cash-flow-backed lack a valuation anchor; underweight the middle.

insights.claim: Buyback-heavy tokens (HYPE, Derive, Lighter's LIT, Aerodrome) have a fundamental floor because buybacks at constant revenue retire more supply as price falls; e.g., Hyperliquid buys back three times as much HYPE at $30 as at $90 at $2-3M/day revenue.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Revenue-plus-buyback tokens let investors tolerate being early; store-of-value tokens lack that floor.
insights.quote: hype is buying three times as much hype back when it was trading at you know 30 bucks than when it's trading at 90 bucks

insights.claim: Hyperliquid ushered in a regime change where the expected marginal buyer of a token is the protocol itself via automated buybacks, which the guest credits for his outperformance over the past year.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Screen for tokens with programmatic revenue buybacks relative to market cap.
insights.quote: the marginal buyer of your token is your token essentially

insights.claim: Institutional investors show interest when shown crypto assets trading at 2-3x P/E (as Pump was), but recoil at pitches for alternative store-of-value altcoins, viewing them as flash-in-the-pan meme coins.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Cash-flow tokens are the more viable institutional on-ramp versus alt SoV narratives.

insights.claim: Zcash has the perfect narrative setup (privacy, quantum resistance, fears of rising US socialism) but is a crowded consensus crypto trade lacking a large external buyer akin to a Saylor; with everyone already long, it needs price action to attract new capital.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Crowded positioning raises drawdown risk; size accordingly or wait for better bids.
insights.quote: you just don't really have like a sailor for Zcash right now

insights.claim: Zcash's quantum-resistance pitch may backfire with normies by educating them that quantum is a problem for Bitcoin more than promoting Zcash's benefits.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Marketing narratives can spill over as Bitcoin FUD rather than Zcash demand.

insights.claim: Unlike Bitcoin's ossified code, Zcash has an active dev team and planned upgrades, increasing attack surface; the Orchard 'infinite mint' scare showed that uncertainty undermines it as a store of value.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Protocol-change risk is a structural discount on SoV candidates other than Bitcoin.

insights.claim: The host's Zcash thesis: wealthy outsiders like Naval are skipping Bitcoin for Zcash for privacy, and Bitcoiners occasionally defect a few percent into a new asset (as with ETH in 2021), so it takes little capital to lift Zcash to 3-5% of Bitcoin's market cap.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Frame ZEC upside as a ratio to BTC market cap driven by small hedges from large holders.
insights.quote: it actually doesn't take too much external cap capital to get Zcash up to like three, four, five% of Bitcoin

insights.claim: The guest agrees billionaires are taking Zcash as a first crypto exposure, but argues that 'just in case' allocation has likely already happened more than people expect; the edge is estimating what share is already priced in.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Assess how much of the high-net-worth privacy bid is already in the price before chasing.

insights.claim: Zcash's bull case resembles a 'king of the wasteland' bet on a Bitcoin black swan (quantum, seizures, Satoshi's coins moving), but in such an event correlations go to one, so Zcash would likely crash too before rallying fastest; it is crash insurance only zoomed out.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Don't hold ZEC as a short-term hedge against BTC tail events; expect to rebuy lower after the shock.

insights.claim: Because Zcash is highly reflexive and has no revenue, it can trade like a memecoin to any valuation, unconstrained by multiples; within a year it is likely either near $200 or near $5,000 rather than compounding steadily.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Bimodal outcome distribution favors convex instruments over linear exposure.
insights.quote: if you zoom out in a year, it's going to 200 or it's going to 5,000

insights.claim: The guest prefers options over perps for leveraged Zcash upside because the path will include 60-80% drawdowns that would liquidate perp longs; conversely, Zcash calls trade rich, making covered-call writing against spot attractive.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Buy ZEC calls for levered upside without liquidation risk, or sell rich calls against spot if neutral.

insights.claim: Zcash options are expected to see major adoption growth, following a path similar to HYPE options.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Venues listing ZEC options could gain volume share.

insights.claim: Perps only express long or short delta (or funding farming), while options always offer a tradable view (long/short vol, targeted upside, deep OTM gamma), so the guest runs longer-term theses through options and trades delta in and out with perps.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Combine options for thesis expression with perps for cheap tactical delta adjustments.
insights.quote: with options, there's always a trade to be had

insights.claim: Example of tactical perp use: Bitcoin dipping to about $72K was an attractive quick perp long scalp back toward $76K, a move not worth crossing options spreads for.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Short-horizon scalps belong in perps where spreads are tighter.

insights.claim: The guest prefers relative-value via upside trades (sell HYPE calls around $100 against spot, buy LIT calls) and avoids shorting either Hyperliquid or Lighter because HYPE can print 20-30% candles.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Express pair views through call overlays, not short legs, in high-upside-volatility tokens.
insights.quote: I hate the concept of of being short either in this market.

insights.claim: Crypto rewards Lindy front-runners with higher revenue multiples (explaining why Lighter has traded at lower multiples than Hyperliquid), opposite to TradFi where smaller high-growth names get higher multiples, because investors expect incoming TradFi money to crowd into the number-one asset.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Don't assume multiple convergence between category leaders and challengers.

insights.claim: Pump trades at a low multiple because investors doubt its meme-coin revenue is durable and suspect current extraction comes at the expense of future revenue.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Cheap multiples can be justified by perceived revenue decay.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's USDC treasury-yield revenue (via the stablecoin deal) is durable, ARR-like income deserving a higher multiple than cyclical trading revenue, which Lighter lacks.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Separate recurring yield revenue from cyclical fee revenue when valuing exchange tokens.

insights.claim: The guest sees Lighter as the better hold over 3-6 months, partly because Hyperliquid was perceived as somewhat Trump-aligned (lobbying, CFTC friendliness) and post-midterm Lighter may have a cleaner path to US regulatory clarity; with equal CFTC clearance, Lighter could pop a couple multiples versus 20-40% for Hyperliquid.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Short-term relative tilt toward LIT on US regulatory catalysts.
insights.quote: Hyperlid was at least a little bit of a Trump bet

insights.claim: A bear case for Lighter's US-focused strategy: as with Kalshi/Polymarket VPN usage, US traders who want perps may already be using them, so the 'untapped US market' could be smaller than assumed.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Discount US-onshoring upside in exchange-token valuations.

insights.claim: Long term the guest trusts the Hyperliquid team more and would rather hold all HYPE than LIT through a one-to-two-year 'coma', seeing HYPE as a multi-year BNB-like compounder.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: HYPE as core long-duration holding; LIT as tactical trade.
insights.quote: I would rather go into a coma for a year or two holding all hype than all lit.

insights.claim: The host argues Hyperliquid fits the Binance model because crypto is inherently offshore, while Lighter targets onshore retail (hence its Robin Hood partnership matters), since institutions will likely stay in options rather than perps.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Offshore liquidity leaders may capture more value than compliant onshore challengers.

insights.claim: Liquidity is a far bigger moat than features: the guest concedes Lighter has better UI/UX but still trades mostly on Hyperliquid for deeper liquidity, though Lighter fills on majors are improving; and Hyperliquid altcoin liquidity remains an order of magnitude below Binance.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Track order-book depth/fill quality as the leading indicator of exchange share shifts.
insights.quote: liquidity is so much more of a moat than people realize

insights.claim: Because of buyback-and-burn, HYPE could trade at the same market cap in five years yet at a multiple of today's price; the guest thinks HYPE can still do multiples but is no longer a 10x asymmetric trade.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Value HYPE on per-token terms with supply shrinkage; temper asymmetric return expectations.
insights.quote: You're you're longing the price, right? You're not you're not long the market cap.

insights.claim: TradFi markets trade and settle in the quadrillions, so both Hyperliquid and Lighter capturing a few percent would mean orders-of-magnitude growth; valuation comps to ICE, CME and Binance are apples-to-oranges given new users like Asian demand for US-equity perps.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Exchange-comp valuation caps may understate on-chain exchange TAM.

insights.claim: Crypto perps have hit saturation (volume and OI still not fully recovered since the 10/10 crash a year ago), while crypto options are at a hockey-stick adoption stage with far more untapped volume.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Allocate to options-venue exposure over perp-venue exposure for growth.

insights.claim: The guest's mental model: crypto options volume could 5-10x next year while Derive's 85-95% share of daily notional/fees falls to perhaps 55-60%, still a much bigger absolute business.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Long Derive as the cleanest options-market proxy despite expected share loss.
insights.quote: derive might only be 55 or 60% of the market share next year, but the market share might be 5 to 10x higher

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's risk engine is poorly suited to native options; HIP-4 enables only prediction-market-based 'bastardized' options, so native Hyperliquid options are likely 9-12 months out versus Lighter's 2-3 months.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Lighter gains first-mover options exposure; being long crypto options partly implies LIT over HYPE.

insights.claim: Small options protocols like Dime (Paradex) and Synapse (Hyper Call) trade at low-eight or even seven-figure market caps, and new entrants like Variational are targeting structured products, an under-researched niche in crypto.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Small-cap options tokens are high-risk optionality on a growing market.

insights.claim: Crypto is at 'peak career risk' for allocators: with the AI bubble partly popping and a political regime shift, betting crypto rallies while equities fall is hard to defend, keeping institutions away and leaving assets dislocated and cheap.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Career-risk-driven underallocation can create asymmetric entry points.

insights.claim: An AI cooldown may be accommodative for crypto: institutions weren't bearish on crypto, just apathetic because AI and semis were the higher-beta tech play; risk-chasing capital exiting AI may look for a new home in crypto.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Watch for flows from AI/semis into crypto as momentum rotates.

insights.claim: Crypto already front-ran the tech sell-off with Bitcoin well below its all-time high, so the key question is whether this marks the end of the crypto bear market; falling 10-year yields and an end to war abroad would argue for loading risk assets.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Build a top-down 3-6 month view keyed to 10-year yields and geopolitics.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid and Zcash may be 'permabull' crowded positions that would be the last assets to hold if crypto sells off substantially.
insights.speaker: Cool Crypto (guest)
insights.so_what: Crowding risk in consensus longs; monitor positioning.
